check.correction:
The defect is real, but three parts of the claim are overstated.

1. It is not a clean regression from main. The mechanism is unchanged on main, and main already elides: BABEL TIME renders '03:30...' and ID '34530...', NWR AREAS '020121,...'. It is still CL1's to own, since the D2 font change caused the worsening and nothing else in the audit covers it.

2. It is transient and order-dependent, not permanent. Leaving the page and coming back, or first showing the sub-tab after rows exist, re-measures and everything fits. The claim's 'never re-measure' holds only while the table stays on screen from empty — which is the normal case for a page the operator sits on.

new_verified.title: Alerts drawer acknowledges the wrong alert when a new one arrives: selection is restored by row index
new_verified.poc: reaudit/d1-sweep/poc2.py section (a), live hub: publish alert 'A: IMSI catcher suspected', open the drawer (row 0 = A selected), publish 'B: GNSS jamming detected', press Enter via hub.handle_key. Output: after B arrives selected row 0 -> B; after Enter: [('B: GNSS jamming detected','acked'), ('A: IMSI catcher suspected','NEW')]. ack_selected (panels.py:378-379) indexes the store by the view's current row; FeedTable._restore_row (feed.py:92-97) keeps the row number across a model reset while new alerts are inserted at index 0.
new_verified.impact: An alert the operator has not read is marked acknowledged and drops out of the unacknowledged count, while the one they meant to acknowledge stays NEW. The highlight does move to the new row, so it is visible if the operator looks again, but a keypress already in flight lands on the wrong alert. The existing D10 test acknowledges with no arrival in between.

check.reproduction:
Wrote and ran my own PoC against the branch working tree (a716e2f), offscreen, live hub (demo=False) built with the test module's _hub helper: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-daltonhayes-SentryHub/f893c360-320b-4c7c-9dc4-e3ab8ef11055/scratchpad/reaudit/verify-alert-ack/poc.py

Scenario 1 (the claim): publish alert A, open the drawer with the 'a' key, publish alert B, send a real Return key event via QTest.keyClick.
Output:
  drawer visible True row 0 A: IMSI catcher suspected
  after B: row 0 B: GNSS jamming detected
  [('B: GNSS jamming detected', 'acked'), ('A: IMSI catcher suspected', 'NEW')] unacked 1 topbar 1 NEW

Scenario 2 (my variant, no in-flight keypress needed): alerts X, Y, Z in the store, operator selects row 2 (X), alert W arrives, then ack_selected().
Output:
  sel X
  [('W', 'NEW'), ('Z', 'NEW'), ('Y', 'acked'), ('X', 'NEW')]
Y was acknowledged instead of X.

Cause, confirmed by reading:
- palisade_qt/panels.py:292 AlertStore._on_event inserts new alerts at index 0.
- palisade_qt/panels.py:378-379 ack_selected passes the view's current row number to store.ack.
- palisade_qt/kit/feed.py:88-96 _remember_row/_restore_row keep the row number, not the row identity, across the model reset that AlertsDrawer.refresh triggers.
- palisade_qt/shell.py:357-358 routes Enter in the drawer to ack_selected.

Test coverage: the only test touching this path is tests/test_cl1_screen.py:723-744 (test_alerts_persist_until_acknowledged_not_capped_at_three), which does selectRow(0) then ack_selected() with no arrival in between, so it cannot catch this.

Scope: the alerts drawer is the CL1 fix for D10 (plan/briefs/CL1.md:85, "a drawer with history and acknowledge"), so this is a defect in CL1's own new code, not another cluster's finding. grep of AUDIT_INDEX.md for "alert" returns nothing relevant, and D10 in the audit (p21) only describes the old three-item cap.

Read-only check: git status after the run shows only the pre-existing untracked .claude/.
check.correction:
The claim is accurate; three refinements.

1. File path: the row-restore code is in palisade_qt/kit/feed.py:88-96, not "feed.py:92-97".

2. The impact is slightly understated. It is not limited to a keypress already in flight. Whenever the cursor sits on any row N and an alert arrives, the highlight silently moves to a different alert (the one now at row N) and stays there, so a later, deliberate Enter or ACKNOWLEDGE SELECTED click also hits the wrong alert (scenario 2: X selected, Y acknowledged).

3. Severity: Medium is right. The wrongly acknowledged alert stays in the history marked "acked", the highlight shows which row is selected, and the intended alert stays NEW, so nothing is lost and no emission or gate is involved. The cost is that an unread alert drops out of the topbar unacknowledged count. I considered High (a display the operator relies on) but it needs an arrival between selection and acknowledge and is recoverable from the drawer.

A fix needs a regression test that publishes an alert between selection and acknowledge.

banner: PANIC — TX disarmed · no engagement was open · 3 child process(es) killed

So 1.5 s after PANIC the banner says 3 killed while 3 of 5 processes are still alive: both pipeline members of A and the TERM-ignoring B. Only the sh wrapper and the plain argv child died.

Cause, from the code:
- shell.py:59-67: child_pids uses `pgrep -P`, which lists direct children only.
- shell.py:70-75: _terminate sends one SIGTERM and returns True if os.kill did not raise. There is no killpg, no SIGKILL follow-up and no wait or liveness check.
- shell.py:294-295: the count is the number of signals sent without error, reported as "child process(es) killed".
- The pages' own stop paths use killpg on the session (e.g. prowl.py:476); PANIC does not call them.

Regression coverage: tests/test_cl1_screen.py:616 (test_panic_key_disarms_ends_engagement_and_kills_children) replaces both seams with fakes (`_list_children = lambda: [4242, 4243]`, `_kill = lambda pid: ... or True`), so no test exercises the real child_pids or _terminate and none would catch this.

Scope: PANIC "kill child processes" is a CL1 brief requirement (plan/briefs/CL1.md:75-76) and the report claims D8 CLOSED citing shell.py:277. It is not one of the 93 findings and not G11 (CL2), which is about a capability ticket for the executor. CL1-report.md:83-85 discloses only that PANIC "sends SIGTERM to every direct child ... which includes receive decoders"; it does not disclose that the decoders behind the sh wrapper survive or that the count is unverified.

Not checked: I ran this on macOS /bin/sh only, not on the Debian dash target. I did not run the full test suite, as it was not needed for this claim.
check.correction:
The core claim is accurate and High is right: the PANIC banner and alert state a kill count that is false, on the one safety control an operator will take at its word, and the error over-reports rather than failing safe.

Three points are overstated or need narrowing:
1. "Any future transmit tool spawned as a pipeline would keep emitting" is speculative. Today every shell=True spawn in palisade_qt is a receive decoder (prowl, babel, atlas APRS/AIS). The one active-tool path, recon.py:56, is subprocess.run(argv), a direct child that does get SIGTERM. TX disarm and engagement end both worked in my run. The present impact is receive pipelines left running and holding the dongle plus a false count, not an emission, so this is not Critical.
2. "Leaves rtl_fm / multimon-ng running" is inferred from the process shape using sleep|cat stand-ins on macOS; no real decoder was run. Dash on the Debian target also forks each pipeline element, so the same result is expected there, but I did not execute it.
3. The implementer partly disclosed the design (direct children, SIGTERM only) at CL1-report.md:83-85 and raised it as open question 5 at line 148. What is undisclosed and wrong is that the real decoders are grandchildren and survive, and that "killed" counts signals sent.

Additional detail: a plain argv child such as PRISM's (prism.py:77) is killed correctly. The line reference is right: shell.py:294 for the count, with the root cause at shell.py:59-75.

The uConsole Fn layer is resolved in keyboard firmware and does not arrive as a Qt modifier. This matters only if a modifier is physically held or latched at the moment of the press. Low on its own.

Reproduced independently with my own script, not the other auditor's. | Injected raise | TX / engagement | Killed | Banner | Alert | Top-bar slots right after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| none (baseline, children 11,12,13) | disarmed / ended | [11, 12, 13] | visible, "PANIC — TX disarmed · engagement Op ended · 3 chil…" | 1 | NONE / OFF |
| `_kill` on pid 11 | disarmed / ended | [] (12 and 13 never attempted) | none | 0 | "ACTIVE · 10.0.0.*" / "ARMED" |
| `_list_children` | disarmed / ended | [] | none | 0 | "ACTIVE · 10.0.0.*" / "ARMED" |
| `chrome.reset` (child 77) | disarmed / ended | [] | none | 0 | "ACTIVE · 10.0.0.*" / "ARMED" |
| RECON page `on_gate_changed` | disarmed / ended | [77] | none | 1 | NONE / OFF |
| `eventbus.bus.publish` (not in the claim) | disarmed / ended | [77] | none | 0 | "ACTIVE · 10.0.0.*" / "ARMED" |

- **Exception escapes:** v2.py shows it leaving the event filter: "Error calling Python override of QMainWindow::eventFilter(): boom".
- **Stale slots self-heal:** at t+0 the slots read ('ACTIVE · 10.0.0.*', 'ARMED'); at t+900 ms they read ('NONE', 'OFF'). The banner never appears.
- **Code:** palisade_qt/shell.py:293-300 (`chrome.reset()`, the kill comprehension, `bus.publish`, `state.poll()`, `_gate_changed()`, `_show_banner`) has no try/except. Only the txguard and engagement steps at 281-292 are guarded.
- **Tests:** tests/test_cl1_screen.py:616 and :647 cover only the happy path; no test injects a failure after `engagement.end()`.
- **Scope:** PANIC is new in CL1 (the brief's D8 "one PANIC key"). It is not one of the 93 findings and is not assigned to another cluster; the CL1 report mentions only G11 (nothing registered to kill).
check.correction:
The mechanics of the claim are accurate, but Medium overstates it; I rate it Low (robustness hygiene).

- **No natural trigger shown.** Every reproduction needs a non-OSError injected into a seam. With the shipped seams, `_terminate` calls `os.kill`, which raises only OSError subclasses (caught); `child_pids` catches OSError and SubprocessError; `chrome.reset` is a dict `.clear()`.
- **The only realistic path is the mildest one.** A page's `on_gate_changed` (three implementations) or `state.poll()` could raise in production. Both run after the kill and the alert, so on that path only the banner is lost: I measured killed=[77], alerts=1, slots correct.
- **The two safety-relevant steps always run first.** TX disarm and engagement end completed in every case.
- **The claim understates the stale display slightly.** The TX slot also reads "ARMED" until the next poll, not just the ENGAGE slot. This is a false "still live" reading, not a false all-clear, and it self-corrects within about 500 ms.
- **One more unguarded step.** `eventbus.bus.publish` raising has the same effect (no alert, no banner).

The line reference is slightly loose: the unguarded block is shell.py:293-300, with the kill comprehension at 294. The suggested fix is still worth making because it is cheap: wrap each post-end step separately, kill per pid inside a try, and always reach `_show_banner`, with a fault-injection regression test.

check.correction:
The claim is real and the file/line references are accurate. Three adjustments:

1. "During a burst of alerts every Enter hits the wrong item" is overstated. The wrong item is hit only when an alert arrives between the operator choosing a row and pressing Enter / clicking the button. An Enter pressed with no arrival in between acks the row shown.

2. "Acked unseen" needs qualifying. The highlight stays on the same screen row and the new alert's text is drawn under it, so an operator looking at the drawer at that instant can see the selection now reads the new alert. The alert is not deleted: it stays in the history as grey "acked", and the top-bar count stays non-zero (for the older alert the operator had already read). The harm is a race plus a wrong NEW/acked state, not data loss.

3. The claim understates the reach: it is not limited to row 0 / the newest alert. With a lower row selected by mouse, an arrival re-points the selection to the adjacent newer alert (run B: selected B1, acked B2), and the same happens through the ACKNOWLEDGE SELECTED button, not only Enter.

Severity: High is defensible and I keep it, though it sits at the Medium/High boundary. It is an acknowledge state the operator relies on, it is wrong in the unsafe direction (a newer, possibly higher-severity alert is marked handled), and it needs no unusual input, only an alert arriving while the drawer is open. It is not Critical: nothing emits, and the alert stays visible in history. Someone weighting the timing dependence and the retained history could reasonably call it Medium.

The claim is real and reproduces exactly; High is right on the given scale (a PANIC banner and bus alert the operator relies on state a kill that did not happen; TX is still disarmed via txguard, so it is not a bypass to emission and not Critical).

Corrections and additions:

So PANIC makes things worse than not killing at all: before PANIC, worker stop() would have killed the whole group; after it, the rtl_fm-style member is orphaned to init and keeps holding the dongle until someone kills it by hand.
2. Slightly misattributed: the respawn reference prowl.py:294-295 is in FmWorker, whose pipe is fm.Pipe (prowl.py:60-64), not the shell=True pipeline. I did not execute the respawn path for any worker; that part remains code-reading only, as the claim itself says.

4. Partly disclosed by the implementer: CL1-report.md:83-85 says PANIC "sends SIGTERM to every direct child of the app, which includes receive decoders. Their workers may respawn them", and line 148 says PANIC kills receive pipelines "(it does now)". That last statement is false for pipelines, as shown. The report does not disclose that the "N killed" count is wrong.
5. Run on macOS only; not run on the uConsole's Debian sh. The mechanism (signal to the wrapper pid only, pipeline members in the same process group left alone) is not platform-specific, but that is inference, not a measurement.

check.correction:
The PARTIAL verdict and its core hold: no TX or gate assertion was weakened, the five named tests have teeth, and the two gaps are real. Four details are overstated or imprecise.

1. **"Relaxation (1)" is not a relaxation.** `hub.stack.count() == len(QT_PAGES)+1` still measures lazy page creation (1 on a fresh hub, 8 after opening all). The old `len(hub.pages)` could not be kept because the dict now carries alias and `:inner` entries (14). Reading `_worker` before the pump is harmless: the worker is created synchronously in `start()`, and `isRunning` is still checked after the loop.

2. **"Lifecycle coverage of the detector threads was lost by the move" is only narrowly true.** On main the soak test never watched the detector workers either (4 of 17 threads on both revisions). The only main-side protection was `test_recon_open_pump_close_no_leaked_threads`, which catches a stop() that drops both the loop and the list reset, and nothing subtler. The accurate statement is that SweepApp did not inherit even that weak test.

3. **"The per-app leak assertions are always True" is slightly too strong.** They are vacuous only while stop() still executes `self._workers = []`. They do fail when the whole stop block is removed, as the main-side mutation showed.

4. **The SWEEP leak mutation is not silent.** No named test fails, but the pytest process crashes (segfault rc=139 in my runs, abort rc=-6 in the claimant's), so CI would go red, just without attribution and at an unstable point. "After 66 passing tests" is not a stable figure; mine crashed after 143, and after about 200 in the full-suite run.

One thing the claim understates: the "ACTIVE — " / "REFUSED — " prefix at panels.py:242 is new on this branch. Main set the message to `why` alone and coloured it live or warn by `ok` (recon.py:546-547). The branch colours both outcomes amber, so the untested prefix is now the only cue in the message line that distinguishes a refusal. It still fails safe: the engine refuses, the hero stays "—", and the RECON cards stay locked (covered by tests).

Severity is Low on the audit's scale: these are test-hygiene gaps with no gate or display defect behind them. They fall under the CL9 "with each cluster" obligation, so they are in scope for CL1 follow-up as two missing regression tests: a SweepApp start/pump/stop test that captures the workers before stop(), and an EngagePanel refusal test.

The claim is accurate on every point I checked, including the line numbers (topbar.py:269, 279, 283; audio.py:60, 72-73) and both surviving mutations. Three qualifications:

1. Severity: Medium is right, but it sits on the Medium/High boundary. A MUTE button that latches while audio keeps playing is a display an operator would rely on, which is the High wording. I keep Medium because the trigger is conditional (a mixer binary installed but its calls failing, e.g. no PipeWire/Pulse session or no default sink) and nobody has shown that this state occurs on the uConsole. The report itself marks section 9 "not verified on the device". If the device's launch context turns out to have no reachable audio session, this becomes High.

2. "The operator is told the handheld is muted when it is not" is only demonstrated at the widget-state level (isChecked() True, slider value 75). I did not render the strip to confirm how visibly the checked state is drawn.

3. The claim understates one adjacent case: for pactl, if get-sink-volume succeeds but get-sink-mute fails, get() returns muted=None (audio.py:81-82) and topbar.py:272 treats that as not muted. An unknown mute state is therefore shown as unmuted at startup. Same root cause, same missing test.

Not pre-existing in this form: on main the slider is connected to nothing and there is no mute, which is the audited section 9 finding. The branch narrows "moves but changes nothing" to the mixer-fails case and adds a new false-muted indication that main could not produce. Section 9 audio should therefore be PARTIAL, not CLOSED.

new_low_unverified.title: The slider-to-mixer wiring (the original audio defect) is not under test: the regression test calls the slot by hand
new_low_unverified.poc: Mutation a_slider_signal_unwired: replace kit/topbar.py:247 `self.volume.valueChanged.connect(lambda _v: self._vol_timer.start())` with `pass` -> tests/test_cl1_screen.py + tests/test_palisade_qt.py all pass. Mutation a_debounce_timer_unwired: replace topbar.py:245 `self._vol_timer.timeout.connect(self._apply_volume)` with `pass` -> all pass. test_volume_slider_and_mute_drive_the_real_sink does `tb.volume.setValue(75); tb._apply_volume()` (lines 881-882).
new_low_unverified.impact: The audit finding was literally 'the volume slider was connected to nothing'. That exact state can be re-introduced and the suite stays green, so by the project rule the wiring is not regression-protected. A qWait past the 120 ms debounce instead of the direct call would pin it.

new_low_unverified.title: test_every_page_key_parses_to_a_real_key tests Qt, not PALISADE
new_low_unverified.poc: Lines 464-467 build QtGui.QKeySequence(str(i)) for i in 1..8 and assert Qt parses it, then assert QKeySequence('10').toString() == ''. Nothing from the app is called except len(CALLSIGNS) <= 9. The shell never creates a QKeySequence for page keys - it matches ev.text() in '12345678' (shell.py:365). Removing that branch (mutation d8_no_digits) leaves this test passing; it is test_keyboard_only_walk_reaches_every_page_and_subtab that fails.
new_low_unverified.impact: The CL1 report lists this as the regression test for the D8 'QKeySequence("10")' PoC. It cannot fail for any change to the application's key routing, so it should not be counted as pinning anything; the keyboard-walk test is the real pin.

new_low_unverified.title: SWEEP's four detector threads have no lifecycle test after moving out of RECON; a leaked-thread regression surfaces only as a process abort
new_low_unverified.poc: probe3.py on a716e2f (hub demo, every name in ALL_CALLSIGNS opened as test_hub_soak does): watched: ATLAS AtlasDemoWorker, PRISM SweepWorker, PROWL ScanWorker, BABEL DecoderWorker, all others None (SWEEP None) - 4 watched, 17 QThreads running, 4 of them DetectorWorker. Mutation x_sweep_stop_leaks_workers (delete the stop/quit/wait loop at sweep.py:57-60): no test fails by name; log shows 66 passing dots then 'Fatal Python error: Aborted', rc -6, stack in palisade_qt/worker.py:42 for each leaked thread. grep 'SweepApp' tests/ -> only two uses, both calling _on_counter directly.
new_low_unverified.impact: The base-class R1/R3 guarantee does not cover SweepApp's own _workers list, and CL1 moved those threads there without a test. On the unmodified branch the hub does close clean (probe3: 'running after close: []'), so this is a coverage hole, not a live leak.
